rationale: Both candidates are technically detailed and well-evidenced, but Y engages more directly and more deeply with the PR's actual central controversy — the cudagraph_mode/talker_mtp_accepts_per_row_generators design that GT reviewers (gcanlin, R2-Y) flagged, going further by showing the seed-reproducibility fix is silently broken even at batch size 1 (CUDAGraphWrapper replay behavior) and that talker_mtp_graph_safe=True is unsound on NPU — effectively root-causing the Wallbreazzz NPU crash thread rather than just noting the yaml patch exists. X covers adjacent ground (duplication of the runner's wrap decision, seed-limitation documentation, NPU yaml lacking rationale) but stays at a more surface/consolidation level and spends much of its budget on test-coverage and doc-staleness findings not present in GT. Both are concrete and actionable with file/line citations and suggested diffs, giving Y a moderate edge on recall/precision and a slight edge on actionability.
